subject: Unable to see PO line details after Workday activation
messages:
From: Sung Electronics <procurement@sungelec.com>

Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Can't view PO line items after accepting Workday invite

Hi Neha,

We accepted the Workday onboarding invitation this morning and completed the registration, but when we open the PO (PO-12345) in the portal it only shows the header (PO number, total amount) and the line items section is blank. The downloadable PDF has all the lines but the portal UI is empty.

Attached: screenshot of the portal (sungelec-registration-screenshot.png) and a copy of the PDF we downloaded (PO-12345.pdf). We tried Chrome and Edge. Cleared cache, tried incognito — same result. Our team is blocked from matching the invoice lines to shipments.

Could you help?

Thanks,
Sung Park

procurement@sungelec.com

Hi Sung — thanks for the quick details and the attachments. Sorry for the interruption here. We saw a few similar reports where the portal UI hides line items if a locale/currency parsing step fails during the vendor profile sync.

Quick asks so we can triage:
- Can you confirm the locale and default currency you selected during registration? (e.g., en_US / USD, en_GB / GBP, ko_KR / KRW)
- Which browser + version? You mentioned Chrome and Edge — if you can paste the version that helps.
- If possible, please try downloading the invoice PDF from the portal and confirm whether the line totals match (you said PDF shows lines).

I’ve looped in Marcus (platform) and Olga (onboarding infra). Marcus/Olga — if this is a Workday mapping problem we should: 1) confirm vendor locale is set correctly in the vendor profile, 2) check the ingestion job that normalizes PO lines for Workday-to-portal display, and 3) temporarily provide Sung a CSV extract of lines so they can proceed.

Sung — once Marcus/Olga confirm what they need, I’ll coordinate with you on the workaround.

Best,
Neha
Manager, Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Can't view PO line items after accepting Workday invite

Neha / Olga — I pulled the ingestion job logs for vendor sungelec (vendor id VE-8892). Summary: the daily normalization job ran at 03:02 UTC on 2028-05-10 and completed with non-fatal warnings. The warnings show a locale parse mismatch for three numeric fields (unit_price, tax_rate, quantity) where the incoming payload used comma as decimal separator (e.g., "1,234") while our normalization expected dot. That will cause the frontend formatter to interpret the lines as invalid and hide them.

Workday's vendor feed for APAC partners occasionally sends numbers using locale-specific separators depending on the vendor's region settings. If Sung selected ko_KR or another locale during registration but their feed still uses comma separators (common for some EU locales), we get an inconsistency.

Actions I recommend:
1) Olga: can you attach the ingestion log slice and the raw payload for VE-8892 so we can send to Workday support? I put a private ticket WD-9931 in the internal tracker and will paste the logs there.
2) Quick workaround: expose a downloadable CSV of parsed lines (I'll generate it) so Sung can match invoices now.
3) Longer term: update the normalization to detect and normalize comma vs dot separators based on vendor locale or an auto-detect heuristic.

Assigning to Olga to run the workaround and reach out to Workday if needed.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior SRE, Inference Platform

Subject: Fwd: Can't view PO line items after accepting Workday invite — logs and payload

Hi Workday Support — forwarding an issue affecting Sung Electronics (vendor id VE-8892). The vendor reports that the portal UI shows no PO line items for PO-12345, though the attached PDF contains the lines. Our initial investigation indicates the Workday vendor feed contains numeric fields with comma decimal separators which our normalization pipeline didn't map correctly, causing the frontend to hide malformed line items.

Attachments included for triage: workday-request-logs.txt (ingestion warnings), raw-payload-VE-8892.json (excerpt), PO-12345.pdf (from vendor).

Could you please:
- Confirm whether Workday is sending numeric values formatted according to the vendor's locale, and if so which locale metadata is present on the VE-8892 feed.
- Advise whether the feed can be configured to use a consistent decimal separator (dot) for machine consumption, or include locale tags for each vendor payload.

Sung — as an interim measure we have prepared a CSV extract of parsed lines and attached it to this thread; it should let you map invoices to shipments while we resolve the normalization rule. Please confirm you can open the CSV.

Thanks for the help,
Olga Petrov
Engineering, Onboarding Infra
Redwood Inference
